items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: when his records came out with Chet Baker and Gerry Mulligan I used to play along with those

ctx.x: You were talking about playing without amps and the physicality of it.

Oh yeah well the first gig somebody came up — my brother was famous in jazz at that time. And I was in around ninth grade or tenth grade. And somebody came up to me and said, “Are you Carson’s brother?” I said, “Yeah, yeah.” He says, “You play the bass?” I go, “Yeah,” I lied. And I used to — he had left a half-sized bass there that I used to fool around with and then when his records came out with Chet Baker and Gerry Mulligan I used to play along with those, not knowing anything. All I knew was how it was…
Sorry for the interruption — That term, “not knowing anything” I think is an important thing to say. Let me see if I can pin you down. What do you mean by that? “Not knowing anything?”
